Name: Acehnese
Status_comment: Pronominal clitics on the verb follow S=A≠P; no ergative flagging (Asyik 1987).

Name: Apatani
Status_comment: Nominative (zero)-accusative ('mi') case system: A and S unmarked, P marked (Abraham 1985:35-38).

Name: Nêlêmwa
Glottocode_note: The coded source (Bril 2002) describes Nêlêmwa; bala1316 (Balade/Nyelâyu) was a mis-assignment. Nêlêmwa-Nixumwak is kuma1276.

Name: Pitu Ulunna Salu
Status_comment: Campbell (1989:47): 'absolutive/ergative case inflections are limited to the arguments represented by pronominal affixes on the verb stem. There are no case markings on nouns.' Ergative alignment is a property of indexing only.

Name: Berta
Status_comment: Absolutive/nominative distinction is positional, not based on transitivity; no ergative flagging (Andersen 2003).

Name: Bierebo
Status_comment: S and A are marked identically (subject prefixes); no ergative flagging (Budd 2009:161).

Name: Bilibil
Status_comment: An optional postposition mos occurs on subjects, especially when the object is fronted; the few available examples show it on A only, which is insufficient to establish an ergative marker (Dempwolff 1909). Grambank codes GB409=1.

Name: Bugis
Status_comment: Ergative-absolutive alignment is realised by pronominal proclitics/enclitics on the verb (indexing), not by flagging; free pronouns and NPs are not case-marked (Hanson 2003:59-60, 126, 153).

Name: Kakataibo
Glottocode_note: caca1251 is not a valid Glottocode; Kakataibo is cash1251 (Cashibo-Cacataibo) in Glottolog 5.3.

Name: Cemuhî
Status_comment: S and A are marked identically by personal modalities; no separate A flag (Rivierre 1980:65, 185).

Name: Coeur d'Alene
Status_comment: Full-NP A arguments take the 'oblique' marker only in some contexts (e.g. when an overt P is animate; Doak 1997, ex. 420, 433); person is otherwise expressed by verbal affixes and proclitics. Whether oblique-marked A constitutes ergative flagging is unresolved.

Name: Lisu (Dechang dialect)
Status_comment: Active-stative (split-S) flagging: le33 marks A and agentive S, non-agentive S is unmarked like P (Yu 2007). Split-S systems fall outside the operational definition used in this release (ERG flagging on the default intransitive class), and the coding is derived from the same source as hual1240.

Name: Emai
Status_comment: No ergative alignment of flagging; the "subject concord" marker of imperfective transitive clauses is not a case marker (Schaefer & Egbokhare 2017:37-42; 2026 review).

Name: Momu
Status_comment: Nominative-accusative; the clitic =m marks objects/obliques, not A (Honeyman 2016; Blake 2007).

Name: Fulniô
Status_comment: Ergative alignment is found only in indexing (third-person singular pronominal clitics on the verb); pronouns and full NPs show no ergative flagging (Costa 1999:145-146, 309; 2026 review).

Name: Lisu (Central/Lipo dialect)
Status_comment: Active-stative (split-S) flagging: le33 marks A and agentive S, non-agentive S is unmarked like P (Yu 2007). Split-S systems fall outside the operational definition used in this release, and the coding is derived from the same source as dech1234.

Name: Huastec
Status_comment: Person marking on the verb resembles an inverse system; there is no flagging of nouns or pronouns, hence no ergative flagging (Kondić 2012; 2026 review).

Name: Hula
Status_comment: No ergative case morphology described (Short 1938).

Name: Iaai
Status_comment: Personal markers of the agent series mark both S and A; no ergative flagging on pronouns or NPs (Ozanne-Rivierre 1976:148-149, §4.37-4.39).

Name: Kamula
Status_comment: The putative ergative -ta is optional, also marks intransitive subjects and attaches to non-argument elements; Routamaa (1994:75) states it 'cannot be described as' ergative.

Name: Karajá
Status_comment: Free pronouns are identical for S and A (nominative pattern) and full NPs are not case-marked; S and A are distinguished from P by word order and verbal morphology (Ribeiro 2012:51, 54, 174, 191-192).

Name: Karitiana
Status_comment: No case morphology exists (Everett 2006:304); Everett explicitly rejects an ergative analysis of free pronouns (p. 365).

Name: Lihir
Status_comment: No ergative alignment of flagging; the grammar notes only a historical connection with an ergative language (Neuhaus 2015).

Name: Lijili
Status_comment: Nominative-accusative; no ergative flagging (Stofberg 1978).

Name: Limos Kalinga
Status_comment: The grammar analyses the language as an 'active language' (Shibatani's typology), not ergative; subject marking does not follow ergative alignment (Ferreirinho 1993, §1.3).

Name: Lipo
Status_comment: Coded from Yu (2007), a description of Lisu, which describes the agentive marker le on A and on agentive S (split-S flagging). Four ERGON entries derive from this source; whether Yu (2007) describes Lipo at all must be checked.

Name: Lisu
Status_comment: Coded from Yu (2007), which describes the agentive marker le on A and on agentive S (split-S flagging; see dech1234 and hual1240). Four ERGON entries (lisu1250, lipo1242, dech1234, hual1240) derive from this source; their classification and identity must be resolved together.

Name: Lushootseed
Status_comment: Salish voice/person-hierarchy system: the oblique marker ?ə marks NPs in several semantic roles and S and A share the subject position (Zahir 2018, §2.1-2.3). Grambank codes GB409=1; the alignment of flagging could not be classified unambiguously.

Name: Maram Naga
Status_comment: Nominative-accusative: S and A take -na, P takes -go (Singh 1984, §2.2.8).

Name: Maranao
Status_comment: Philippine-type voice system; the topic particle 'so' marks the topic regardless of role; no A-specific flag (McKaughan & Macaraya 1967).

Name: Maxakalí
Status_comment: Campos (2009, §9.2.1) analyses the system as tripartite-active: A and agentive S take the postposition -te, non-agentive S is marked by a person prefix, and P is unmarked. It does not instantiate S=P≠A flagging.

Name: Marori
Status_comment: The clitic =i marks the undergoer (P and patientive S); A and agentive S are unmarked. This split-intransitive pattern is outside the operational definition of ergative flagging used here (Arka 2012:152-154).

Name: Northern Qiang
Status_comment: An optional agentive suffix -wu marks non-topical A only and cannot mark S; the grammar describes the system as nominative-accusative (LaPolla & Huang 2003, §3.2.3). Under the v1.1 scope definition (optional A-only marking counts as ergative flagging) this pattern qualifies as optional ergative flagging; the sheet, coded under the earlier stricter criterion, must be recoded before the language can be classified.

Name: Pendau
Status_comment: Ergative-like marking arises when the genitive marks the agent in inverted (undergoer-voice) clauses; pronouns are not flagged (Quick 2007). The status of this voice-conditioned pattern as ergative flagging is unresolved.

Name: Yaminawa
Glottocode_note: yami1258 is not a valid Glottocode (typo in v1.0.1 CLDF build); Yaminawa (Yaminahua) is yami1256.
